metaDescription: Inosa abaca is an abaca variety. About 23 months to harvest. See its ratings and traits. Compare it with others. Free guide.
excerpt: Inosa is a registered abaca variety, also sold or known as NSIC Mt 02. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2017 as NSIC 2017 Mt 02. It takes about 23 months from planting to the first harvest.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Inosa abaca takes about 23 months from planting to the first harvest. That is 1.5 months longer than the average of the 3 abaca varieties with a day count, 21.5 months. Count the months from planting, and plan the harvest for a dry stretch when you can.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [Fusarium wilt](/diseases/fusarium-wilt).

The pests and diseases that hit abaca fields most often: [Banana aphid](/pests/banana-aphid), [Banana bunchy top](/diseases/banana-bunchy-top), [Banana weevil](/pests/banana-weevil), [Fusarium wilt](/diseases/fusarium-wilt). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** Fiber yield listed as about 1,270 per hectare.
**Fruit:** High fiber tensile strength, about 57 kgf/g m.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: PhilFIDA's strong fiber abaca, singled out for pulp and paper because of high pulp recovery. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Inosa abaca

Abaca needs rain spread through the year and a little shade. Pick a variety by fiber yield and strength, and plant clean suckers or tissue cultured plantlets. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is NSIC Mt 02 the same as Inosa?
items.a: Yes. NSIC Mt 02 is another name for Inosa, registered as NSIC 2017 Mt 02. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 23 months from planting to the first harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Inosa?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
